title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: OTIS BUILDS A BIRD
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Otis Fairley, sixty-two, a shipyard welder in Mobile, Alabama.
For forty years, he built ships. Then he promised to build a giant pelican.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BIG PROMISE
segments.quote: Imagination is more important than knowledge.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: Mobile has America's oldest Mardi Gras, and Otis's street had never entered a float.
At the block meeting, he blurted out, I'll build one. Then he stared at a blank page. He was no artist.
His wife Bernice taped a note on the fridge, from Albert Einstein:
Imagination is more important than knowledge.
So Otis drew the silliest, happiest bird he could.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TOO MUCH STEEL
segments.quote: I suppose it is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.
segments.author: Abraham Maslow
lines: Otis built it the only way he knew. All steel. The beak weighed more than his truck.
His neighbor Odette, a retired seamstress, quoted the psychologist Abraham Maslow:
I suppose it is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.
So Otis kept steel for the bones, and let Odette teach him foam and fabric.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HEAD FALLS OFF
segments.quote: Great things are not done by impulse, but by a series of small things brought together.
segments.author: Vincent van Gogh
lines: Three weeks in, Otis rushed and bolted on the giant head in one night.
By morning, it was lying in the driveway, smiling up at him.
Then he remembered the painter Vincent van Gogh:
Great things are not done by impulse, but by a series of small things brought together.
So he stopped rushing. One feather, one bolt, every night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SEVEN O'CLOCK
segments.quote: Inspiration is for amateurs — the rest of us just show up and get to work.
segments.author: Chuck Close
lines: Some nights, after a long shift, Otis didn't feel like a genius. He felt like a nap.
His grandson Marcus texted him a line from the painter Chuck Close:
Inspiration is for amateurs — the rest of us just show up and get to work.
So every night at seven, Otis walked into that garage. Soon the neighbors came too.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: PARADE DAY
segments.quote: A man without mirth is like a wagon without springs.
segments.author: Henry Ward Beecher
lines: Parade day. Halfway down Government Street, the wing motor quit. The pelican froze.
Otis felt his face go hot. Then he remembered the speaker Henry Ward Beecher:
A man without mirth is like a wagon without springs.
So Otis laughed, grabbed a rope and flapped those wings by hand for two miles. The crowd loved it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SECOND PLACE
segments.quote: Happiness lies not in the mere possession of money; it lies in the joy of achievement, in the thrill of creative effort.
segments.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
lines: The pelican took second place. Otis didn't mind one bit. He thought of President Franklin Roosevelt:
Happiness lies not in the mere possession of money; it lies in the joy of achievement, in the thrill of creative effort.
He spent the fifty-dollar prize on pizza for all his helpers. Next year? A flamingo.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Imagine big. Right tools. Small pieces. Show up. Laugh. Enjoy the making.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Imagine big. Use the right tools. Build it piece by piece. Show up anyway. Laugh when it breaks. Enjoy the making.
I tried flapping like a pelican once. My arms quit before the first float.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
